questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I prioritized finding an english-speaking country, while I also wanted to do my exchange in a country far away from Denmark, as these countries are more difficult to travel to

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I just applied through VUW's website and was given a room within a couple of days. At VUW they have both independent living and catered option for student accommodation. The catered option is for young students who have just moved out. I would definitely recommend one of the independent living options, as this is a really good way to get to know other exchange students, as a lot of events are happening every week and a lot of exchange student live in student accommodation. I lived at 222 Willis, and i would recommend either 222 Willis, Everton Hall or Kelburn Flats. You can sometimes feel a little much looked after, as they have 24/7 reception and they do an inspection of the flat half way through, which is a little bit annoying. It is also a little bit expensive, compared to normal rent of rooms in Wellington, but I would still 100% recommend student accommodation, if you want to get to know other exchange students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived both closed to campus and central in the city, so it was nice

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I took only 3 level courses, corresponding to 3rd year courses in the Denmark, but I wish I had taken more 1 level courses as this was possible and the work-load was much smaller on these. The 3 level courses can have a lot of workload during the course: tests, papers and so, that are mandatory and count towards your final grade. 
The level of the courses was a bit lower than in Denmark, as I had already learned some of the content in the courses in courses I had in first and seconds year at home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching was both lectures, tutorials and laboratory work

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Pharmacology, Cell- and Immunobiology, and Cellular Regulation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My favorite of the three courses I had was definitely Cell- and Immunobiology, I found it very interesting with good teachers
Pharmacology I would not recommend, unless you like chemistry

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take more lower-level courses if you want more free time.
Apply for student accommodation if you want to get to know other exchange students. 
Use your free time on exploring the country, it is beautiful (both north and south)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *

questions.answer: Getting to know other exchange student and exploring New Zealand was amazing

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Workload on 3 level courses was a bit much as you dont really want to spend all your time studying while in New Zealand, so learning to prioritizing also exploring the country
